_doc:
READING AND NUMERACY (Phase 064): what a resident makes of written marks and of counts and prices, at the agent view. A written mark is a physical object in the world whose id is a key of WRITTEN_MARKS; its text is authored here (the world holds no text on signs). The reader's literacy tier (LITERACY_TIERS, named by domains/shared_frames.py literacy_tier) chooses how much of the text reaches the resident. Its numeracy tier (NUMERACY_TIERS) chooses how a count or a price is put into words.

SWITCH. READING.enabled defaults to false. Off, the agent view has no `writing` rows and nothing is learned. The reading percept needs the perceiver record of Phase 062, so PERCEPTION.enabled must be on as well.

READING. squiggle: what an unknown word looks like. dark_lights: the light keys in which no mark can be read (or learned). common_numerals: the number words every resident knows. learned_max: the most words a resident can learn from use (a bound on held state; APPROX, a display and memory cap, not a measured figure). learned_kind: the memory kind a learned word is held under.

LITERACY_TIERS. One row per literacy tier, in order. reads: 'words' (the resident sees the words it knows amid squiggles; a mark with no known word reads as unreadable), 'short' (the short text of the mark), or 'full' (the whole text).

RECOGNITION. A resident recognises a word it has from its trade (RECOGNISED_SEED, by trade name), its own name, the common numerals, and the words it has learned from use. Recognition does not need literacy: a labourer who knows ALE sees ALE on a sign. A resident learns a word when the referent of a mark it has seen (refers_to) is carried or in view and the mark is in sight in the light. Learning is not reading: a learned word does not raise the literacy attribute of the world (APPROX, not modelled here).

NUMERACY_TIERS. One row per numeracy tier, by the lowest level it takes (the level is the world's `capability` attribute, the general reckoning and comprehension of a resident; frames/constants.json). exact_max: a count up to this is said in words (spelled, no digits). few_max: a count up to this (and above exact_max) is 'a few'; above it is 'many'. prices: 'units' (a price is said in the unit the mark gives, a loaf, when the resident trades in it) or 'figure' (the price in coins). The threshold levels are APPROX (authored, not measured).

NUMERACY_UNITS. A unit of trade, its value in coins, and its words. The coin value of a loaf is 2.0, the shop price default of the world (prices.json shop_price, a model default, APPROX).

NUMERAL_WORDS. The spelled numbers: words for 0 to 20, the tens words for 20 to 90, and the words for a hundred and 'and'. Counts above 999 are said as 'many'. No view string carries a digit (agent_view.py rule).

WRITTEN_KINDS. Each written kind (sign, price, notice) has a label and one template per reading mode: `words` (the words amid squiggles, {shown}), `short` ({short}), `full` ({text}), and `unreadable` for a mark with no known word. Which mode a literacy tier gets is LITERACY_TIERS.reads, so a tier can be changed in data. The self-test finds a kind with no template for a mode in use.

WRITTEN_MARKS. Keyed by physical object id. kind names a WRITTEN_KINDS entry; refers_to is the item the mark names (lowercase; it must appear in text). text is the whole text and short the plain short text; {price} in either is replaced by the price in the reader's numeracy words. A price mark also gives price (coins) and unit (a NUMERACY_UNITS key). The prices are authored on the sign, not read from a shop, so they do not move with the market (a limit of Phase 064).

RECOGNISED_SEED. The words a resident of each trade recognises from its trade (keys are TRADES keys). Authored, APPROX.
